origin: Original practice stimulus; reviewed axis/unit derivation

data.unit_rule: Vertical-axis unit divided by horizontal-axis unit; angle/count ratios may be dimensionless.
data.model_limit: Idealised practice data only. Do not infer that every real dataset is exact, that every line passes through the origin, or that the gradient is automatically a familiar constant.

gradient_meaning: The slope is temperature rise per second, 0.08 °C/s. For 0.100 kg of water with c = 4200 J/(kg K), the water gains energy at mc(dT/dt) = 33.6 W. A roughly 35 W heater allows about 1.4 W for losses in this idealised example; voltage alone does not set its power.
aim: test water temperature as heating time increases at a fixed heater setting
arrangement: A 6 V immersion heater rated about 35 W, a suitably rated current-limited 6 V supply and leads, 0.100 kg water in an insulated beaker, thermometer, stirrer and stopwatch
